body.statement:
Fix \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), and condition on any projected pilot pair \((\bar\pi,\bar\mu)\) produced by \(\mathsf M_{h,k,J_\pi,J_\mu}^{\mathrm{DP}}\).  Let \(\Pi_{h,k}\) denote componentwise Lebesgue \(L^2(C_h)\)-projection onto the span of \(b_{h,k}\).  There is a coefficient vector \(\vartheta_\tau\in\mathbb R^{p_\gamma}\) such that, with
\[
 g=\pi_Q-\bar\pi,\qquad r=\mu_{0,Q}-\bar\mu,
 \qquad t=\tau_Q-\rho_h^{\mathsf T}\vartheta_\tau,
\]
one has \(\rho_h(x_0)^{\mathsf T}\vartheta_\tau=\tau_Q(x_0)\), \(\lVert\vartheta_\tau\rVert_2\le C\), and \(\lVert t\rVert_{L^\infty(C_h)}\le Ch^\gamma\).  If \((Q^\circ,R^\circ)=\mathbb E_Q[(T_{*,Q},T_{*,R})\mid\bar\pi,\bar\mu]\) and
\[
 Q^0=\int_{C_h}K_h(x)\rho_h(x)\rho_h(x)^{\mathsf T}
       \pi_Q(x)\{1-\pi_Q(x)\}\,dx,
\]
then
\[
 R^\circ-Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau
 =\int_{C_h}K_h\rho_h\pi_Q(1-\pi_Q)t\,dx
 +\int_{C_h}(I-\Pi_{h,k})(K_h\rho_h g)
                 (I-\Pi_{h,k})(r+\pi_Qt)\,dx,
\]
and
\[
 Q^\circ-Q^0
 =\int_{C_h}(I-\Pi_{h,k})(K_h\rho_h g)
                 (I-\Pi_{h,k})(\pi_Q\rho_h^{\mathsf T})\,dx.
\]
Consequently, with \(\ell_{h,k}=h/k^{1/d}\),
\[
 \lVert R^\circ-Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau\rVert_2
 \le C\{h^\gamma+\ell_{h,k}^{\alpha+\beta}
                  +h^\gamma\ell_{h,k}^\alpha\},
 \qquad
 \lVert Q^\circ-Q^0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C\ell_{h,k}^{2\alpha}.
\]
Moreover, \(\lambda_{\min}(Q^0)\ge\kappa(1-\kappa)\) and \(\lVert R^\circ\rVert_2\le C\).  Every constant in this lemma depends only on \((d,\kappa,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L_\pi,L_\mu,L_\tau)\) and the fixed basis normalizations, not on the pilot dimensions or their realized Gaussian noises.
body.proof_tex:
Because \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}propensity\text{-}holder}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}control\text{-}holder}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}cate\text{-}holder}\) hold.  The metric projections in \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}higher\text{-}order\text{-}learner}\) therefore give
\[
 \bar\pi\in\mathcal H^\alpha(L_\pi;\mathcal X),\quad
 \kappa\le\bar\pi\le1-\kappa,
 \qquad
 \bar\mu\in\mathcal H^\beta(L_\mu;\mathcal X),\quad
 0\le\bar\mu\le1.
\]
In particular, \(g\in\mathcal H^\alpha(2L_\pi;\mathcal X)\) and \(r\in\mathcal H^\beta(2L_\mu;\mathcal X)\).  These conclusions are deterministic after conditioning on the pilots.

Let \(P_\tau\) be the Taylor polynomial of order \(\lfloor\gamma\rfloor\) of the H\"older version of \(\tau_Q\) at \(x_0\), expressed in the tensor Legendre coordinates \(\rho_h\); its coordinate vector is \(\vartheta_\tau\).  Taylor's formula with H\"older remainder gives
\[
 P_\tau(x_0)=\tau_Q(x_0),\qquad
 \sup_{x\in C_h}|\tau_Q(x)-P_\tau(x)|\le C L_\tau h^\gamma,
 \qquad \lVert\vartheta_\tau\rVert_2\le C.
\]
The last bound uses bounded outcomes, which imply \(|\tau_Q|\le1\), and equivalence of norms in the fixed-dimensional polynomial space.

We next compute the population score.  Conditional on \(X=x\), consistency and the definitions of \(\mu_{0,Q}\) and \(\tau_Q\) give
\[
 \mathbb E_Q(Y\mid A,X=x)=\mu_{0,Q}(x)+A\tau_Q(x).
\]
Using \(A^2=A\), one obtains, pointwise in \(x\),
\[
 \mathbb E_Q\!\left[(A-\bar\pi)
       \{Y-\bar\mu-A\rho_h^{\mathsf T}\vartheta_\tau\}\mid X=x\right]
 =\pi_Q(1-\bar\pi)t+gr.
\]
Since \(\pi_Q(1-\bar\pi)=\pi_Q(1-\pi_Q)+\pi_Qg\), this is
\[
 \pi_Q(1-\pi_Q)t+g(r+\pi_Qt).                                      \tag{1}
\]
The clipping maps in the definition of \(T_*\) are identities on the realized kernels, because their radii are the suprema over the ranges containing \((\bar\pi,\bar\mu)\).  Independence of the two records in the order-two kernel and the orthonormality of \(b_{h,k}\) show that its population contribution to the last product in (1) is
\[
 \int_{C_h}\Pi_{h,k}(K_h\rho_hg)\,
                  \Pi_{h,k}(r+\pi_Qt)\,dx.
\]
Self-adjointness and idempotence of \(\Pi_{h,k}\) give the Pythagorean identity
\[
 \int uv-\int(\Pi_{h,k}u)(\Pi_{h,k}v)
 =\int\{(I-\Pi_{h,k})u\}\{(I-\Pi_{h,k})v\}.              \tag{2}
\]
Substituting \(u=K_h\rho_hg\) and \(v=r+\pi_Qt\) into (2) proves the first displayed identity.  Applying the same calculation to the matrix score, and using
\[
 \pi_Q(1-\bar\pi)=\pi_Q(1-\pi_Q)+\pi_Qg,
\]
proves the identity for \(Q^\circ-Q^0\).

It remains to bound the two remainders.  The resolution-ordered boundary-corrected tensor spline system in the corrected declaration of \(b_{h,k}\) has mesh width comparable to \(\ell_{h,k}=h/k^{1/d}\).  To verify the needed approximation rather than assume it, partition the rescaled unit cube at the last complete resolution preceding the \(k\)-th basis function.  On each tensor cell subtract the Taylor polynomial of order \(\lfloor u\rfloor\) of a function \(v\in\mathcal H^u(L;C_h)\).  The H\"older remainder is at most \(CL\ell_{h,k}^u\); the polynomial lies in the spline space because its coordinatewise order is below the declared spline order.  Squaring and integrating over the \(h^d\)-volume cube, and then using the best-approximation property of orthogonal projection, gives
\[
 \lVert(I-\Pi_{h,k})v\rVert_2
 \le CLh^{d/2}\ell_{h,k}^u.                                  \tag{3}
\]
For \(K_h\rho_hv\), perform the same cellwise subtraction after multiplying the Taylor polynomial by \(\rho_h\).  The product remains in the declared spline space, and \(K_h=h^{-d}\) on \(C_h\), whence
\[
 \lVert(I-\Pi_{h,k})(K_h\rho_hv)\rVert_2
 \le CLh^{-d/2}\ell_{h,k}^u.                                 \tag{4}
\]
Equations (3)--(4), Cauchy--Schwarz, and contraction of an orthogonal projection yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left\lVert\int (I-\Pi_{h,k})(K_h\rho_hg)
                  (I-\Pi_{h,k})r\,dx\right\rVert_2
 \le C\ell_{h,k}^{\alpha+\beta},\\
 &\left\lVert\int (I-\Pi_{h,k})(K_h\rho_hg)
                  (I-\Pi_{h,k})(\pi_Qt)\,dx\right\rVert_2
 \le C\ell_{h,k}^{\alpha}\lVert\pi_Qt\rVert_2h^{-d/2}
 \le Ch^\gamma\ell_{h,k}^\alpha,\\
 &\left\lVert\int (I-\Pi_{h,k})(K_h\rho_hg)
                  (I-\Pi_{h,k})(\pi_Q\rho_h^{\mathsf T})\,dx
   \right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C\ell_{h,k}^{2\alpha}.
 \end{aligned}                                                \tag{5}
\]
The first integral in the score identity is bounded by \(Ch^\gamma\), since \(\int K_h=1\), \(\rho_h\) is uniformly bounded, and \(0\le\pi_Q(1-\pi_Q)\le1/4\).  This proves the two asserted remainder bounds.

Finally, the canonical tensor Legendre normalization gives
\[
 \int_{C_h}K_h(x)\rho_h(x)\rho_h(x)^{\mathsf T}\,dx=I_{p_\gamma}.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}overlap}\) therefore implies
\[
 v^{\mathsf T}Q^0v
 \ge\kappa(1-\kappa)\int K_h(v^{\mathsf T}\rho_h)^2
 =\kappa(1-\kappa)\lVert v\rVert_2^2.
\]
Thus \(\lambda_{\min}(Q^0)\ge\kappa(1-\kappa)\).  The bound on \(R^\circ\) follows either directly from the range restrictions, (2), and projection contraction, or from \(R^\circ=Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau+(R^\circ-Q^\circ\vartheta_\tau)\), the already proved bounds, and \(0<\ell_{h,k}\le h\le r_0\le1/4\).
